briefing.headline: Burnham's EU stance fuels UK‑EU debate, US midterms reshape Congress
briefing.overview: The UK prime minister argues a referendum is needed to re‑join the EU, while US Democrats secure a historic House majority. Parallel debates on devolution and judicial independence add further complexity.

stories.title: Burnham says EU re‑entry must be put to a referendum
stories.what_happened: Prime Minister Andy Burnham told the Guardian that rejoining the EU would be "unthinkable" without a public referendum and criticised former Tory leaders for opposing the debate. He also described his predecessors as "stuck in the past".
stories.why_it_matters: The comment highlights the executive's role in shaping foreign policy and the constitutional requirement for parliamentary approval of major treaties. It also raises questions about the balance of power between the prime minister and Parliament under the UK constitution.

perspectives.label: Supporters argue
perspectives.text: Burnham's call for a referendum respects democratic legitimacy and gives the public a direct say on a major constitutional change.

perspectives.label: Critics argue
perspectives.text: Opponents say the demand could destabilise the UK's post‑Brexit settlement and undermine the government's ability to negotiate swiftly.

perspectives.label: From the right
perspectives.text: Conservative commentators warn that repeated referendums erode parliamentary sovereignty.

key_term.definition: A direct vote by the electorate on a specific political question.

stories.exam_use: Use as evidence in an essay on the executive's influence over constitutional change and the role of referendums in UK politics.

stories.title: Welsh Greens push for separation from English party
stories.what_happened: The Welsh Green Party announced plans to split from its English counterpart by 2035, seeking an independent Welsh political identity. The move was reported by BBC Wales.
stories.why_it_matters: The split illustrates party fragmentation and the impact of devolution on party structures, a key topic in the AQA study of political parties and regional politics.

perspectives.label: Supporters argue
perspectives.text: An independent Welsh Green Party can better represent Welsh environmental priorities.

perspectives.label: Critics argue
perspectives.text: The division may weaken the overall Green movement's electoral strength across the UK.

perspectives.label: From the left
perspectives.text: Progressive voices see the split as a step towards greater regional autonomy.

key_term.definition: The transfer of powers from the central government to regional or local bodies.

stories.exam_use: Cite when discussing how devolution influences party organization and regional representation.

stories.title: US Democrats win largest House majority in decades
stories.what_happened: In the 2026 midterm elections, Democrats secured the biggest House majority in a regular election in three decades, according to The Hill.
stories.why_it_matters: The result shifts the balance of power in Congress, affecting legislative agendas and the relationship between the executive and legislature, core to the US government syllabus.

perspectives.label: Supporters argue
perspectives.text: The victory reflects public approval of Democratic policies on climate and health.

perspectives.label: Critics argue
perspectives.text: Republicans warn that such a majority could lead to unchecked partisan legislation.

perspectives.label: From the left
perspectives.text: Progressive groups view the win as an opportunity for bold reforms.

key_term.definition: Having more than half the seats, allowing control of legislative decisions.

stories.exam_use: Use to illustrate how electoral outcomes reshape congressional power dynamics in an essay on US elections.

stories.title: Federal appeals court opens path for Trump to challenge hush‑money conviction
stories.what_happened: A federal appeals court ruled that President Donald Trump can seek to have his hush‑money conviction dismissed on immunity grounds, moving the case to a federal court.
stories.why_it_matters: The decision highlights the role of the judiciary in checking executive actions and the constitutional debate over presidential immunity.

perspectives.label: Supporters argue
perspectives.text: Trump's team says immunity protects the office from politically motivated prosecutions.

perspectives.label: Critics argue
perspectives.text: Legal scholars warn that broad immunity could undermine accountability.

perspectives.label: From the right
perspectives.text: Conservatives view the ruling as a defence of executive authority.

key_term.definition: Legal protection that may shield a sitting president from certain lawsuits.

stories.exam_use: Reference when discussing the separation of powers and judicial review in the US constitution.

stories.title: Welsh government funds National Slate Museum redevelopment
stories.what_happened: The Welsh Government allocated an extra £2.4 million to redevelop the National Slate Museum, as reported by Nation.Cymru.
stories.why_it_matters: The funding demonstrates devolved fiscal powers and the ability of the Welsh administration to invest in cultural projects, linking to the AQA topic of devolution.

perspectives.label: Supporters argue
perspectives.text: Investment preserves Welsh heritage and boosts local tourism.

perspectives.label: Critics argue
perspectives.text: Opponents claim the money could be better spent on public services.

perspectives.label: From the left
perspectives.text: Progressive voices see cultural funding as essential for community development.

key_term.definition: A regional government with powers transferred from the central state.

stories.exam_use: Use as evidence of how devolution enables regional policy decisions in an essay on UK governance.

compare.uk: Burnham seeks a referendum to legitimize a major foreign policy shift, showing the prime minister's influence over constitutional change.
compare.us: President Trump is using the courts to challenge a conviction, illustrating the US executive's reliance on judicial avenues for protection.
compare.insight: The contrast shows the UK executive works through parliamentary consent, while the US executive can directly invoke judicial review, reflecting different constitutional arrangements.

ideas_lens.text: Burnham's call for a referendum aligns with liberal ideas of popular sovereignty and individual participation, echoing John Locke's emphasis on consent of the governed. Liberalism also underpins the US courts' role in checking executive power.

exam_question.question: Assess the extent to which the executive can influence constitutional change in the UK and the US, using recent examples.
exam_question.tip: Compare Burnham's referendum proposal with Trump's use of the courts, focusing on parliamentary sovereignty versus judicial review.
